atlas-my.0113: The employer first gets labour-department approval, then applies; since 1 June 2026 all three categories may bring family. Foreign-owned sponsors need RM 500,000 of paid-up capital.
atlas-my.0114: Since October 2025 foreign employees pay 2% into the EPF pension fund, matched by the employer.
atlas-my.0121: An Employment Pass from Kuala Lumpur does not cover work in Sabah or Sarawak, which run their own immigration.
atlas-my.0123: For remote workers and freelancers with foreign clients only: 3 to 12 months, renewable once.
atlas-my.0126: Thesis research at a Malaysian university uses a student mobility pass through EMGS, 1 to 12 months; research at institutes or companies a Professional Visit Pass. Field research may need government clearance.
atlas-my.0127: PhD and master’s students keep the Student Pass, may bring family, and research assistantships are free of income tax.
atlas-my.0128: Malaysia has working-holiday agreements only with Australia and New Zealand.
atlas-my.0129: Up to 90 days with no work; fill in the free Malaysia Digital Arrival Card within three days before arriving. Repeated border runs to reset the 90 days lead to refusal and a blacklist.
atlas-my.0130: Fill in the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card before you travel. Students apply through Education Malaysia Global Services (EMGS); workers through their employer and the Expatriate Services Division.
atlas-my.0131: Expect to pay 2 months’ damage deposit, 1 month in advance and half a month’s utility deposit when you rent.
atlas-my.0132: Have the lease stamped with stamp duty on e-Duti Setem (MyTax) within 30 days of signing: an unstamped lease is not valid proof of residence for a bank account or utilities.
atlas-my.0133: On arrival you get a temporary special pass, usually 30 days. Your employer or university then hands your passport to immigration for the visa sticker and the i-Kad card, which takes 2 to 6 weeks; meanwhile you cannot leave the country or fly to Sabah or Sarawak.
atlas-my.0134: Register your tax identification number online on MyTax. Until you have spent 182 days in Malaysia, your employer withholds a flat 30%; for arrivals in the second half of the year, more than 14 days abroad on holiday can break the count.
atlas-my.0135: Since 1 October 2025 employees on an Employment Pass pay 2% into the EPF pension fund, matched by 2% from the employer, refundable when you leave for good.
atlas-my.0136: Your employer must cover you under the SOCSO employment injury and invalidity schemes; expatriates are excluded from the unemployment insurance scheme.
atlas-my.0137: Banks (Maybank, CIMB, Public Bank, RHB) refuse accounts on a tourist visa or approval letter: bring your passport with the visa sticker, the i-Kad, a letter from your employer or university addressed to the branch, and the stamped lease.
atlas-my.0138: When you leave for good, the visa cancellation (check-out memo) and tax clearance are needed to withdraw your EPF savings.
atlas-my.0139: Until you have spent 182 days in Malaysia in the year, employers withhold a flat 30% tax.
atlas-my.0140: Malaysia does not accept apostilles: documents need consular legalisation at the Malaysian embassy.
atlas-my.0141: A positive urine test is a crime even if the drug was taken legally abroad; CBD products are banned.
atlas-my.0142: Same-sex relations are criminalised, with prison sentences of up to 20 years.
atlas-my.0143: While your passport is with immigration for the pass sticker, 2 to 6 weeks, you cannot travel abroad or to Sabah and Sarawak.
atlas-my.0144: Employers renewing category II and III passes must file a local succession plan from 1 January 2027; the criteria are not out.
